document_metadata.title: 40、INT. ROCKET HANGAR
document_metadata.summary: Ted, muttering alone, insists he's sane; nurse Stella Barrington offers help, mentions her dying father wants burial on Mercury; Ted acknowledges her father's work and leaves abruptly.

entities.name: Ted presents evidence of faulty wiring in high-temperature conditions
entities.description: Ted holds up a piece of wiring and points out that it is shorting out under high temperatures, attempting to convince Simon of a critical flaw in the system.

entities.name: Simon dismisses Ted's concerns about the wiring
entities.description: Simon rejects Ted's warning about the wiring, claiming it meets all safety specifications and suggesting Ted is overworked and imagining problems.

entities.name: Newspaper boy announces headline accusing Ted of going mad
entities.description: A newsie passes by shouting a sensational headline: 'Shuttle test pilot goes mad!', publicly discrediting Ted's mental state.

entities.name: Technician Jacobs presents flight uniform designs for approval
entities.description: Jacobs enters with drawings of flight outfits and presents them to Simon for review, particularly highlighting the captain's design.

entities.name: Simon rejects studded dog collar design in flight uniforms
entities.description: Simon inspects the uniform designs and angrily rejects the inclusion of studded dog collars, demanding they be removed.

entities.name: Jacobs leaves in a huff after design criticism
entities.description: After Simon criticizes the uniform designs, Jacobs snatches the drawings and exits the scene visibly upset.

entities.name: Ted accuses Simon of sabotaging his reputation
entities.description: Ted confronts Simon, accusing him of deliberately spreading rumors that he is having a mental breakdown to undermine his credibility.

entities.name: Ted collides with Elaine while storming off
entities.description: As Ted turns to leave in anger, he bumps into Elaine, who stops him by holding onto him.

entities.name: Elaine expresses concern over Ted's mental and physical state
entities.description: Elaine questions what is wrong with Ted and suggests he is overworked and pushing himself too hard, urging him to rest.

entities.name: Ted rejects Elaine's offer of a quiet dinner
entities.description: When Elaine offers to cook a calming Italian dinner for them both, Ted angrily rebuffs her, accusing her of being complicit in the conspiracy against him.

entities.name: Ted seizes design plans to prove his claims
entities.description: In a fit of frustration, Ted grabs technical plans from a passing technician and shouts that the evidence of flaws is clearly documented.

entities.name: Simon signals guards to detain Ted
entities.description: Simon gives a silent command for security personnel to intervene, leading to Ted being physically restrained.

entities.name: Guards apprehend Ted as he struggles and rants
entities.description: Security guards grab Ted, who resists and continues shouting accusations while being subdued.

entities.name: Doctor sedates Ted with an injection

entities.name: Elaine protests Ted's sedation
entities.description: Elaine cries out in distress, pleading for the doctor to stop and expressing fear that they are harming Ted.

entities.name: Simon justifies Ted's detention as necessary for mission safety
entities.description: Simon tells Elaine that Ted is a danger to himself and the mission, and falsely claims his behavior harms Middle East peace efforts.

entities.name: Elaine collapses in tears on Simon's shoulder
entities.description: Overcome with emotion, Elaine begins sobbing and leans on Simon for comfort after Ted is taken away.

entities.name: Simon smirks evilly after Ted's removal

document_metadata.summary: The Commissioner confronts Kruger by slamming Clarence Oveur's polka album on his desk, revealing Oveur's unexpected musical persona and escalating tensions over his reassignment.

entities.name: Kruger reports a recent senseless murder to the Commissioner
entities.description: Kruger informs the Commissioner that someone has been senselessly murdered just minutes prior, prompting disbelief and tension in the conversation.

entities.name: Kruger questions how Washington will respond to the murder
entities.description: Kruger expresses skepticism or concern about how federal authorities in Washington will react to the recent murder, escalating the political undertone of the situation.

entities.description: The Commissioner cuts off Kruger's implication about Washington's involvement, emphasizing that matters should be handled locally by 'the boys downtown' and 'the boys down'.

entities.description: Kruger identifies Clarence Oveur as the only other qualified shuttle pilot and commands Jacobs to remove him from his scheduled lunar mission.

entities.name: Jacobs misunderstands Kruger's order as a clothing request and flees
entities.description: Jacobs misinterprets Kruger's command to 'pull Oveur' as a request for a sweater, makes a joke about size, and runs out of the room.

relations.description: Jimmy says 'Do you want to talk about it, Commander?', which is a direct speech act from Jimmy to the Commander. However, the extracted subject is 'Simon', not 'Jimmy'. Since Simon is not the speaker in this utterance, the relation cannot be justified. But given that 'Commander' is used as a form of address and Simon is being addressed as 'Commander', the most plausible valid relation is that someone (Jimmy) speaks to Simon using that title. Since we cannot change the subject, and the text does not show Simon speaking to the Commander, the only defensible rewrite under the constraint that 'Commander' is a Character and the relation must be valid is to interpret the use of the title as Simon being spoken to. However, the speaker is Jimmy, not Simon. Therefore, the original relation incorrectly attributes the subject. But per instructions, we cannot change subject/object. Given the strict constraints, and that 'Commander' is a role used in direct address, the only valid relation type supported is 'speaks_to', but only if the direction matches. Since the extracted subject is Simon and object is Commander, and Simon is not speaking to Commander, this fails. Thus, no valid rewrite can be made that is textually supported. Final decision: drop.
